title: Dustin Freeman - Live Action Roguelike Performance
speaker: Dustin Freeman
summary: Dustin Freeman acts as dungeon master while a second performer plays 'the player' in a live-action, chat-driven roguelike staged on a tabletop set with physical props. The audience picks a class (monk, mage or janitor) and actions; the player dies to an unidentified potion and a trapped doorknob, restarting each time while the set is rebuilt as 'real-time procedural generation'. On the third run as a mage, the player hatches and pockets a dragon, crushes puddings with an unknown wand, dissolves the trapped door with a potion, retrieves the amulet and escapes by calling the dragon back. The performance is comedic, with little explicit design commentary, but it enacts roguelike conventions live.

insights.claim: Dustin Freeman's live-action roguelike stages a roguelike as improvised theatre, with chat choosing actions, a DM narrating outcomes and props rebuilt between levels as 'real-time procedural generation'.
insights.detail: The player chooses among monk, mage or janitor, and level transitions are covered by inventory reviews while the set is rearranged. Freeman jokes that this is what real-time procgen really looks like when the engine forgets to generate some areas.
insights.quote: There is some procedural generation that the engine forgot to do so it is just going to do it kind of live in these areas here

insights.claim: The performance reproduces unidentified-item risk: drinking an unknown pink potion turns the player into a tree, ending the run, while later unknown items (a wand of crushing, a levitation potion, an ice orb) are learned by use.
insights.detail: When chat asks how to identify items, Freeman says 'not yet'. Later he notes the red potion may have randomly regenerated between runs, and many items go unused and unidentified.
insights.quote: You drink the potion and immediately you turn into a tree

insights.claim: In Freeman's live roguelike, the earlier rescued dragon pays off as an escape route from a featureless final room, which a performer explicitly calls Chekhov's gun.
insights.detail: After getting the amulet the player sees no way out; chat suggests calling the dragon, which flies in and carries the player back to the surface, winning the run.
insights.quote: This is called Chekhov’s gun. This will be really rewarding when it works out
